title: The relationship between the coarticulatory source and effect in sound change: evidence from Italo-Romance metaphony in the Lausberg area
language: Italo-Romance varieties: Mormanno/Mittelzone and western/eastern Lausberg-area varieties
token_or_recording_size: 5372 analysed mid-stem-vowel tokens (2752 /e/ + 2620 /o/); additional /i a u/ normalization productions documented
annotation_target: stem/suffix vowel boundaries; F1/F2 trajectories; suffix erosion/centralization; lexical and regional predictors
annotation_provenance: MAUS forced alignment + Praat formant tracking, followed by human correction where boundary/formant errors were found
primary_collection: Paper states around 40% of data were manually corrected for misplaced segment boundaries or mistracked formants; retain corrected production measurements and trajectory outputs, with automatic provenance explicit
annotation_files_available: Primary acoustic database embargoed until 2039; not mirrored
evidence_summary: Primary non-singing production corpus with public primary-derived measurement/dataframe layer and documented manual correction of segment-boundary/formant errors. Restricted audio/database is reference-only.
verified_date: Open Data LMU exposes a 2 MB public Secondary_dataset.zip with analysis dataframes/code and a restricted 1 GB Primary_dataset.zip. Paper reports 35 speakers, F1/F2 extracted with 25 ms window/5 ms frame shift, manual correction of roughly 40% for boundary/formant errors, and 11 equally spaced trajectory points.
